descriptionHtml:

What you get

  1. Red and white leather in weights from 6oz to 18oz
  2. A choice of Lace-Up or Velcro closure

Looking after it

Wipe the white after sessions, since light panels show marks, and keep the gloves out of direct sun to hold the red.

Winning Red & White Boxing Gloves FAQ

Will the white panels on the Winning Red & White gloves stain?

White shows marks faster than red. A damp cloth after each session and air-drying them open keeps the white bright; avoid leaving them in a gym bag overnight.

Are red and white Winning gloves a good first pair?

Yes. It is one of the most popular first-pair colorways because it suits any kit. Most beginners start at 12oz for bag work or 16oz if they plan to spar.

What is the difference between this pair and the Red with White Panel?

This pair splits red and white across the glove, while the Red with White Panel is mostly red with a single white back panel and a blue logo.

Yellow can dull with long sun exposure. Store the gloves out of direct sunlight and wipe them after training to keep the color sharp.

Which weight should I choose for black and yellow sparring gloves?

16oz is the standard sparring weight for most adults. Heavier boxers often move up to 18oz, while 12oz to 14oz works well for pads and bag work.

descriptionHtml:

Is it only for women?

No. It is unisex adult, so anyone who likes the color can use it.

Pinks and reds fade faster in direct sunlight. Keep the gloves in a bag and wipe them after use.

Use 12oz for general training and 16oz for sparring. Lighter weights suit speed work and smaller hands.

Can I get more than one shade?

What wraps and kit match pink boxing gloves?

Black, white and gray kit all work. Pink or white wraps keep the look consistent, and black headgear adds contrast.

Yes, especially for someone who wants gloves that stand out. 12oz is the safest gift weight if you are unsure.

descriptionHtml:
White Winning gloves are for boxers who value a crisp look and honest feedback. White leather shows contact marks and scuffs, so it doubles as a record of where your punches land, but it also asks for care. Here is what to expect before you buy.

What you gain

  • A clean, classic appearance that goes with any kit
  • Visible feedback on knuckle alignment and contact
  • A pair that stands out among dark gear

What it asks of you

Wipe the gloves after each session and air-dry them open. Skip that for weeks and light leather grays in a way that does not fully reverse.

Sizes and closures

From 6oz to 18oz, in Lace-Up or Velcro. For sparring, 16oz Lace-Up is the usual choice; for solo bag work, 12oz Velcro is easy to use.

Lower-maintenance alternatives

Try the Silver & White for a bright look with a little contrast, or the Black for a pair that hides everything. See the Winning gloves collection.

Winning White Boxing Gloves FAQ

Are white boxing gloves allowed in sparring?

Most gyms allow any color for sparring; what matters is weight and condition. Check whether your club asks for 16oz gloves before ordering.

Are white Winning gloves good for photos and ring walks?

Yes. White reads cleanly under ring lights and camera flashes, which is why many boxers save a white pair for events, photos and walkouts.

What kit looks best with all-white gloves?

Black shorts give the sharpest contrast. All-white kit looks clean for photos, and gold or red accents add a fight-night feel.

descriptionHtml:

  • Sparring: 16oz or 18oz, Lace-Up

Winning Black Boxing Gloves FAQ

Are black Winning gloves good for fight-camp training?

Yes. Black is neutral, so it works through any training block. For the bout itself, use the corner color and weight your event requires.

Can I match black gloves with colored hand wraps?

Yes. Black works like a blank canvas, so red, blue or yellow wraps add personality without clashing.

Lace-up or velcro for an only pair?

Velcro is easier if you train alone because you can put the gloves on yourself. Lace-up gives a tighter fit but needs someone to tie them.

descriptionHtml:

Why are red gloves associated with the red corner?

In amateur and many pro bouts, the red corner wears red gloves, so solid red has become the traditional fight-glove color.

Do red Winning gloves suit a red-corner club kit?

Yes. Solid red matches red-corner shorts, headgear and club colors, so many clubs choose red for their red-corner gear.

Red or maroon Winning gloves?

Pick red for the bright, traditional corner look. Pick maroon for a deeper wine-red that hides wear better.

descriptionHtml:

  • Finish: metallic gold across the glove
  • Weights: 6oz to 18oz
  • Closure: Lace-Up or Velcro
  • Care: dry cloth only

Why dry cloth only?

Metallic finishes dull when they get wet. Wipe the gloves with a soft dry cloth after each session and avoid sprays or damp wipes.

Lace-Up or Velcro?

Lace-Up keeps the cleanest line against gold and gives the firmest hold. Velcro is faster when you train alone.

Compare other gold options

For gold as an accent, see the Gold & Pink or the Forest Green & Gold. All gloves: Winning boxing gloves.

Winning Metallic Gold Boxing Gloves FAQ

Are metallic gold gloves suitable for regular training?

Yes, but many boxers keep them for fights, events and photos and use a second pair for daily bag work to keep the finish pristine.

What kit pairs with metallic gold gloves?

Black, white or gold-trimmed shorts work best. Black headgear and wraps let the gold stand out.

What weight metallic gold gloves for a fight?

Bout weights depend on your weight class and the event rules, so check with your coach or promoter before ordering.

Who is it for?

Boxers who like the red-corner look but want a little more definition, and coaches who want gloves they can follow easily during pad work.

Related pairs

Winning Maroon, Yellow & Orange Boxing Gloves FAQ

What does the maroon, yellow and orange colorway look like?

A deep maroon base with warm yellow and orange accents, giving a bold, autumn-toned glove.

Is it brighter than the plain maroon pair?

Yes. The yellow and orange accents make it far louder than the solid maroon gloves.

What kit matches maroon, yellow and orange gloves?

Black or maroon shorts keep the look warm and cohesive and let the glove's accents do the work.

seo.description: Maroon Winning boxing gloves with yellow & orange accents: warm, autumn-tone colorway that stands out. Choose 6oz to 18oz, lace-up or velcro.

descriptionHtml:
Four colors on one glove sounds like a lot, but brown, black, orange and white work together because brown and black ground the design while orange and white lift it. The result is a pair that feels earthy and sporty at the same time.

Matching it with your kit

Black or white shorts let the gloves be the focus. Orange wraps echo the accent color; black wraps keep things restrained. Avoid adding more bright colors, because the glove already carries plenty.

Where it fits in training

  • Speed and pad work: 6oz-10oz
  • Heavy bag and mitts: 12oz-14oz
  • Sparring: 16oz-18oz

Each weight is available with a Lace-Up or Velcro closure.

Care

Wipe down after use and let the gloves air-dry open. The white panels will need occasional attention.

For a simpler brown-and-black look, see the Black & Orange. More designs are in the Winning boxing gloves collection, and complete kits are in Winning boxing sets.

Winning Brown, Black, Orange & White Boxing Gloves FAQ

Why choose brown boxing gloves?

Brown gives a vintage, old-school look that is rare among modern gloves and hides wear well.

What role do the orange and white details play?

They add contrast to the brown and black base so the glove looks layered rather than plain.

Is the brown, black, orange and white pair a good gift?

Yes, especially for someone who likes vintage style. 12oz is a flexible gift weight for general training.

seo.description: Four-color Winning boxing gloves in brown & black leather with orange and white detail: a vintage-style pair. 6oz-18oz, lace-up or velcro.
